chunks: Among them is Muhsin ibn Ghassan ibn Zalih al-Zubaydi, who lived for two hundred and fifty-six years.

key_terms.مُحْصِنُ بْنُ غَسَّانَ: Muhsin ibn Ghassan, the individual mentioned

ai.seo_question: Who is Muhsin ibn Ghassan al-Zubaydi and how long did he live according to Shia historical sources?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi includes Muhsin ibn Ghassan al-Zubadi in his catalog of long-lived figures to demonstrate that extended lifespans are not exclusive to the Prophet Muhammad or the Imams, but are a known historical reality within the Arab lineage. This entry supports the Shia theological concept of *ghayba* (occultation) and divine preservation by providing precedents for individuals living through significant historical transitions, thereby reinforcing the plausibility of the Imam of the Age's prolonged life.
